headlines.description: A strong storm system packing heavy rain and gusty winds pushed through the Bay Area Wednesday. Below is a look at the latest storm-related incidents NBC Bay Area is aware of. Related links: El Niño is here: How to prepare for winter in the Bay Area Weather alerts information from National Weather Service Latest forecast from NBC Bay Area Interactive radar Power outages bay area weather Nov 17 bay area weather Dec 25, 2025 Rain closed business, flooded apartment garages in the Peninsula Stormwater flooded Furniture Innovation at Westlake Center, soaking many of its rugs, according to the owner Eun Soon Ackland. The water also caused extensive damage to her custom furniture, from sofas to beds, which she says she can no longer sell. Garages at an apartment complex in Broadmoor also got flooded. The storm also led to some white-knuckle drivers on Highway 101 and lane closures on I-280 as crews removed a down tree. Check out Marianne Favro’s full report in the video player below. Flooding closed businesses and highways in the East Bay Flooding in the East Bay closed businesses and also created big and, in some cases, costly problems for drivers. In Richmond, water covered Cutting Boulevard for blocks. Mahmood Saleh, the manager of Sam’s Liquor, captured video as floodwaters spilled toward his store. In Oakland, flooding on 18th Street spilled inside the Food Market, forcing businesses to shut down until they can clean up and dry out. In Berkeley, the storm left cars stranded on Ashby Avenue under the overpass, forcing crews to close Highway 13. Caltrans says crews are working to pump out the water but warn drivers not to take chances. Velena Jones has the full report in the video below. Heavy rains impact VTA service VTA reports flooding from heavy rains is impacting multiple VTA bus routes throughout Santa Clara County, causing buses to be re-routed. Passengers should plan ahead and check reroute information on X at @VTAService, and the VTA website VTA.org. VTA said a bus was caught in a flooded pothole at the corner of Stevens Creek and Bascom Avenue in San Jose was able to offload 20 passengers safely around 4:30 p.m. The bus was still on scene and waiting for a tow truck late Wednesday. Flooding across the North Bay Corte Madera was just one of several North Bay cities that contended with rising floodwaters. Watch Christie Smith’s full report in the video player below. Cars stuck in flooding near SAP Center in San Jose The San Jose Fire Department said two drivers got trapped in floodwaters at West Santa Clara Street and Stockton Avenue. One driver, a woman, was rescued and transported to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, according to the fire department. The other driver was also rescued. Check out Robert Handa’s full report in the video player below. Evacuation warning issued for neighborhoods near Contra Costa County fairgrounds Contra Costa County officials issued an evacuation warning due to flooding for people living and working around the county fairgrounds in Antioch, and a school was also evacuated. The warning was later lifted. The warning was issued at about 2:30 p.m. and included the area north of State Route 4, south of West 10th Street, east of Crestview Drive and Auto Center Drive and west of L Street. At 4 p.m., the Contra Costa County Fire Protection District said the Antioch Charter Academy school in the area was safely evacuated. The warning was lifted as of 7 p.m. For zone information, people can visit protect.genasys.com. Streets flooded in El Cerrito and San Pablo Police in El Cerrito and San Pablo are advising motorists to avoid flooded streets and intersections amid heavy rain and stormy conditions. The El Cerrito Police Department is urging residents to avoid intersections at Fairmount Avenue and Richmond Street, Fairmount Street and the Ohlone Greenway, San Pablo and Knott avenues, and Carlson Boulevard and Adams Street near San Pablo Avenue. In San Pablo, a police alert said that Rumrill Boulevard between Dover Avenue and Sutter Avenue, and 14th Street between Dover and Sutter avenues are flooded. Additionally, parts of 15th Street, 14th Street, and Rumrill Boulevard are completely closed. Lengthy flight delays at SFO A ground delay program is in effect at San Francisco International Airport because of strong winds, with departing flights being delayed by an average of more than three hours, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. The FAA’s National Airpace System Status website early afternoon showed SFO with average delays of 186 minutes for departing flights. The delays are expected to be in effect through Wednesday night. More than 13,000 Bay Area PG&E customers without power PG&E estimates that 13,828 customers are facing power outages in the Bay Area because of heavy rain and stormy conditions as of noontime. More than 4,000 customers are without power in the North Bay, and more than 3,000 each in the Peninsula and East Bay regions, PG&E said. In the South Bay and San Francisco, 1,800 and 700 customers are experiencing power disruptions, respectively. PG&E had said more than 18,000 customers were without power earlier Wednesday morning because of the stormy weather. “The adverse weather can result in trees, limbs, and other debris falling into power lines, damaging equipment, and interrupting electric service,” the utility company said in a statement. PG&E is cautioning that downed power lines can be highly energized and touching them is “extremely dangerous.” Residents should report downed power lines immediately by calling 911 and then PG&E at 1-800-743-5002. Flooding and roadway hazards in South San Francisco The city of South San Francisco said there was flooding and hazardous road conditions in several areas of the city, especially near Highway 101 and Interstate 280. Several Richmond streets closed due to flooding The city of Richmond said several streets are closed because of flooding. The closed streets include: Cutting Boulevard at Harbor Way Cutting Boulevard from Harbor Way Street to South Ninth Street Cutting Boulevard at Stege Avenue Cutting Boulevard at South 37th Street South Cutting Boulevard at Canal Boulevard 1001 Canal Blvd. and southern section Marina Way between Ohio and Bissell avenues Barrett Avenue underpass at Amtrak MacDonald Avenue underpass at Amtrak Carlson Boulevard at South 47th Street 38th Street at McBryde Avenue Marina Way South between Wright and Hall avenues South 37th Street and Wall Avenue Hilltop Lake Park Essex and Seventh Street Marina Way Parkway between Regatta Boulevard and Meeker Avenue South 12th Street and Cutting Boulevard South 23rd Street between Cutting Boulevard and Ohio Avenue Richmond Parkway and Barrett Avenue Wine Street and Cutting Boulevard 23rd Street and Garvin Avenue Atchison Village – end of Curry Street and West Chanslor Avenue Residents can visit richmondca.gov for additional information on storm preparedness and local contacts for assistance. Waymo puts a pause on service Waymo has paused service in the Bay Area due to the stormy weather. Flooding closes intersection in Berkeley Berkeley police are telling people to avoid the intersection of Ashby Avenue and Bay Street because of extreme flooding in the area. Police issued the advisory at about 10:55 a.m. and said the area will remain closed to traffic until further notice. Flooding reported in Sausalito The Sausalito Police Department on Wednesday morning said that heavy rain and high tides are causing flooding in low-lying areas along Bridgeway and the city’s waterfront. Crews from the Sausalito public works, police and fire departments are working to manage roadways and advise residents to avoid traveling if possible. People should not drive or walk through flooded roads. Updates can be found at emergency.marincounty.gov. Tree falls onto car in San Jose A tree toppled over onto a car in the Cambrian neighborhood in San Jose. No other information was immediately available. A tree is seen down on top of a car in San Jose. (Nov. 18, 2026) Hanging tree limb impacting Highway 92 traffic in Half Moon Bay Cal Fire crews are responding to a hanging tree limb that has shut down one lane of westbound Highway 92 in Half Moon Bay. Major flooding on I-280 in San Francisco The California Highway Patrol reported major flooding on southbound Interstate 280 at Geneva Avenue in San Francisco. Flooding reported in Corte Madera and Larkspur The Central Marin Police Authority is warning of flooding in Larkspur and Corte Madera. In Larkspur, Creekside Drive is closed at Larkspur Plaza Drive and at Creek View Circle. In Corte Madera, Lucky Drive between Doherty Drive and Fifer Avenue is closed, Seawolf Passage at Paradise Drive is closed and Golden Hind Passage at Seawolf Passage is closed. As of 9:50 a.m., the California Highway Patrol reported flooding on southbound Highway 101, just south of Madera Boulevard in Corte Madera. The right lanes are affected and motorists should expect delays. Updates can be found at emergency.marincounty.gov. Widespread storm-related ferry service cancellations The San Francisco Bay Ferry on Wednesday morning reported it is experiencing widespread storm-related cancellations. For service information updates, visit sfbayferry.com/bayalerts. Flooding shuts down roads in South San Francisco Roadways in the area of Produce Avenue and Beacon Way, near the southbound Highway 101 on-ramp, are closed until further notice, authorities reported Wednesday. Drivers should avoid the area and use alternate routes. For more information, visit ssfca.gov/emergency. Flooding and tree down in Santa Rosa The Santa Rosa Fire Department shared video footage of a car stuck in flooding along the side of a road. The video also showed crews clearing a downed tree. Trees into power lines in San Mateo, Santa Cruz counties Cal Fire said it was responding to several calls of trees into power lines in San Mateo and Santa Cruz counties. Flooding in Mill Valley In the North Bay, rain intensified Wednesday morning, with flooding expanding at the Manzanita parking lot in Mill Valley. Another area of flooding was reported farther down the road, where cars were seen driving through the water. Drivers are being urged to watch for ponding and isolated flooding, whether caused by the storm or a combination of storm and tidal flooding. Flooding in Sebastopol In Sebastopol, flooding was reported at a post office parking lot on Petaluma Avenue. Floodwaters reached bumper level on one of the postal vehicles. San Francisco prepares for possible flooding Flooding is a concern in San Francisco along the Embarcadero. The city installed flood barriers along the Embarcadero from Howard to Mission streets in response to the last coastal flood warning and to prevent flooding from happening again. ‘Inclement weather’ shuts down San Francisco Zoo The San Francisco Zoo will be closed Wednesday for both daytime admission and ZooLights due to inclement weather, the zoo said. The zoo provided the following statement: “If you’re wondering how the animals fare – it often depends on the species. Some animals are secured indoors for safety reasons, including the threat of tree limbs coming down, others may choose to be outdoors if they have access. Others may opt to wallow in the mud, or like our penguins, take to the pool to swim, or hunker down in their burrows! We apologize for any inconvenience. Stay safe – and dry!” This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.
